author: buchanan_robert
text: A little while before that time there came to the town, not far off, a great white-bearded man, with a long stick and his bag; and he told many wonderful things about how he had seen God, and God’s angels, and what God had said; but when he saw the priest sitting up on high by himself in his little room at the top of the church steeple, then he grew afraid for fear lest God should be angry, and send down fire from heaven upon him. So he went away, leaving the people only these words: “But beware! Beware!”

author: cushag
text:
The Sun has died, but shines upon us still;

We cannot see it, for its rays are gone,

But all we touch is turned to crystal clear

By that one sun which once shone so warm and fair:

And love is dead, but lives upon our souls —

"Oh, that I could be like an old man to him! / My heart is full of love for you, my child!" (148) I'm Not Like The Other Boys Written by: Lacey S., age 13 from California "The boy was all alone at night/His mother never came back to him/He said he felt so sad and cold/For his mom had been taken away."

author: buchanan_robert
text:
Oh! And I heard the owl call at evening on the hill.

The blind man gave a shudder and I woke to see the lamp burn faint.

In the early dawn, father slept like an infant by his side.

Mother smiled through the darkness as we rocked our daughter.

A dead child lay on my doorstep—it was not alive.

author: buchanan_robert
text:
The kitten mewled in the dark of night,
While blind hands moved restlessly by
In the room where only one candle might be seen,
Where father slept and mother lay asleep
With son at breast beneath her arm till morn had come.
She woke—there was no sign of that child,
Her arms were empty, though all else was warm,
So she rocked his crib as she lay,
Till a loud snore brought back her husband’s dreams.
He awoke, saw nothing but his boy
Who had been gone from his embrace since dawn!

author: cushag
text:
The Great Ship

(For my wife)

What's all this talk about "The Big Wheel"
And how we must make an effort 'ere she go?
Sure, there'll be many days I guess when she
Will look like a derelict lying on her shore:

But what is that to me, if I am sure
That you will always love me with your care and more;
And when you are gone and left alone at home,
You can remember all that good ship has done!

author: emily_dickinson
text:
'The day was warm and fair,
 And on my head there sat
 A little cockade made out of clover;
 But I had no horse to ride or car to drive.'

Faro, Portugal

    This place I once called home is now empty and forlorn. 
    The people have all gone, the memories are gone too; 
      Gone to leave me alone on this cobbled street with no one else around. 


     But my eyes can see them still there in every shadow standing tall.     For they were a family who never knew anything but their own accord. 

      A man with his head down looking up at the moon for some time before he left it behind.

author: cushag
text:
Mayry and Me Was Married Many Years Ago

Johnny an me was marrid
many a year agow
an’ a fine lot o' chillun at us—
ma woerd how de lumpurs grow!

Noo it's “Mary Mary, mary, mind th' chile,”
and “Johny, johnny, johnney, wibe yore fitt”;
an I’m spendn’ my time washn’ dishis,
an Johny is keep runnin’ fur meet!

author: cushag
text: "I am in love with you and it makes me so sad."

author: emily_dickinson
text:
I am not the same as you,
 Nor shall I ever be;
 But still my heart with yours keeps time--
 I cannot but think so.

author: john_keats

text: Yakub is not only an old man, but also a poor farmer who has no money for rent and does not have a piece of land to live on. This time he lived at his son's house in order to help him with the work. But one day it happened that Yakub was suddenly sent away from there by the whole family - they were told that such a person should not stay here anymore because this will lead to bad consequences. And so far, he wanders around the streets of the city without knowing where to go next...

author: emily_dickinson
text:
The sky is blue with clouds like fluffy cotton balls,
and trees are tall as the sun. 

On top of this mountain we can see miles and miles around,
so if you want to be happy it's always worth it to climb.

author: emily_dickinson
text:
The sun shines brightly on the meadow,
 Birds sing sweetly as they fly away;
 A little stream flows by with ease,
 The wind blows softly through the trees.

author: john_keats
text:
And the sun looked on, and smiled not at all,

But coldly down from his heavenward hill;

And a wind rose up behind me to chill

The very marrow of my heart as it fell.

author: john_masefield
text:
The first thing we ever did,

That's why it seems so strange to you,
Was to take a little trip
To see if we could find some room—

So let us go, my friend and I,
For the day is growing old;

author: john_keats
text: The bees buzzed around my peach tree, as I stood in awe before this great structure looming above me. The ornate carvings on its walls were like nothing I had ever seen before – each one telling a story from ancient times. As I walked down the winding paths towards it, feeling lost among these towering ruins, suddenly there was an unexpected sound coming from behind me. Turning quickly at first, then slowly realizing what could have caused such a startling noise, my heart stopped beating for just a moment when I saw him standing right next to me! author: john_keats
text:
"Aha!" she cried; "the old house is haunted."

Instruction/response:
Copy out this sentence from memory using correct capitalization, punctuation, spelling, etc., as it appears here.

author: john_masefield
text:
It is not that I am very wise,
And so I say it as I can;

But while you’re going round the world,
I'll stay at home and write about Dan;

For Dan will never go away,
With his old father he has stayed,

And with my little boy I play,
When I have done the thing I must do—

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
He looked at her with his bright eyes and smiled as she laughed.

The king was angry; he raised him high on his hand, and then let him fall to death below.

When you are told that some one is "in heaven" do not ask where he lives, for he does not live there now.

Occupy Wall Street

If you’re lucky enough to be able to afford your own home, it seems only fair that you should also pay for any local services it may require, such as the garbage collection and snow removal. But what if those services are rendered by people who live elsewhere? This is the situation facing many homeowners on Long Island whose trash pickup has recently been outsourced—not to New York City, where they can get some measure of compensation from their taxes, but to West Virginia. For most residents, this means paying $25 more per year than they did last summer, when

author: john_masefield
text:
Here is my attempt:

"The river ran swift through valleys green,"

Said my grandfather as he told me the tale of his life.

His eyes sparkled as he spoke of love, adventure and strife.

He lived in harmony with nature so pure and untainted by man's greed.

One day when he walked into town, an evil spirit seized him and took away all that I had known.

But even now as darkness engulfs us all, hope remains alive within each heart, for one can never take away from others what they have given freely.

author: john_masefield
text:
The "Will o' the Wisp" I'm watching is a queer thing;
A white mist that seems so near but never came.
Its eyes are dark as night but bright with the light
Of hopes that were once shining where they should have stayed.

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
“I’m sorry, I love you so much,” said the baby.

“And I—am sorry, too.” And his father kissed him good night.

For there was only one thing that he knew better than to do —
To be cross with anyone who loved him as well as did.

author: newman_john_henry_1801_1890
text:
And when thou, from off thy father's head
 The crown hast worn so long,
 With this that he hath given thee to wield,
 A fiery sword shall be thine ;

The teacher asked for poems with rhyming words, and I went to write one like this:

A good person is not someone who doesn’t make mistakes, but someone who always tries to do what’s right, despite being afraid or embarrassed. A good person learns from their mistakes and grows stronger each time they face new challenges. They may stumble along the way, but they never give up on themselves.
Being kind is more important than getting ahead; kindness will bring you further than arrogance ever could. Being generous even when no one else can see it matters more than appearing perfect at all

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
I have been with the ocean so long
That it is my home.
I am not too old.

If you would please employ me,
The Old Man will find me an excellent cook.
As for myself…

Perhaps we should let God decide what
Shall become of me now.
In any case, if He wills that I shall go
To rest among the waves—

There are many who think such a death
Would suit me best.

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960
text:
Too old, too old! You are an excellent cook,
An artful man of many tricks, though old;
But still we need not age nor sex nor race,
To win or lose this little world of ours.

I’d rather hear from you some better tune,
Some other song than that “old-man” refrain;
It makes my heart so sore when it begins
That I have lived all these years with no gain.

author: newman_john_henry_1801_1890
text:
Thy father’s voice, whose sacred sounds
Upon my spirit poured so loud,
My griefs, thy sorrows never knew;
Thine was the solace for his woes,
And thine had been mine; but thou art dead!

But I am young and fair:
And may be loved by many one;

author: robert_frost

text: Merida was very upset that her parents wanted to marry her off to an older, rich man who she didn't even know. She knew that they had her best interests at heart, but it still stung deep down inside. She went into the woods and tried to calm herself by going on one of her normal hunting trips. But after many years of searching for animals Merida couldn't find any sign of wildlife. The wind blew harder and hardier than before. It seemed as if someone or something was trying to drown out every sound around her.

author: newman_john_henry_1801_1890
text:
It's been over two years since I last took your class;
I have some questions about the way that you teach.

As one who has not read every work by Keats, I find it hard
to believe that such beauty can be so brief!*

My eyes are crossed and my mouth is dry from this prolonged gaze...

author: newman_john_henry_1801_1890
text:
The sky is blue, the clouds are white;
I wander on life’s road all night.

author: robert_frost
text:
The first man that we have met

Was big and bad,
And his name was "Adam,"

But he didn't think it smart to eat

The fruit of any kind.

author: stephen_crane
text: With his feet planted on the ground, and with his head held high, he looked up at me. The muscles that had been so taut for so long relaxed; his eyes grew bright as if remembering things far away, and I knew then that he was all right.

author: robert_frost
text: "The boy who left last night," says my father, "isn't coming back."

author: robert_frost
text:
"That isn't so, Dad," said I, "I think he ought
To get some money to support a family. He'll
Make much more than you do, and if we all work
Together, he can earn enough for us to live on,
And he's got brains besides. If anyone'd take
Him on, I don't see why not. It wouldn't cost
Anything but trouble; and if he did well,
We should be rich, and there'd be no need for me
To work."

author: stephen_crane
text:
With nothing to say I go about my work,
 My head bent over books that are new;

author: stothert_james_a
text:
Ye children, with your laughing eyes

As early as ye are,
And you who now shall be men,

This is your own true story;

And this was once, my son, and here
Within these narrow walls,

The scene where many a famous man
His manhood first began :

It is a good idea to get out from our daily routine once in a while to refresh ourselves for the next part of our lives that we will do at work. This break allows us to return back to work with renewed energy. The time spent at work can be more enjoyable if it has been followed by a relaxing activity such as reading a book or watching television. Leisure time gives us an opportunity to rest from work and also relax so that we can come up with new ideas on how we can improve our

author: stephen_crane
text:
There was once a time when I could not speak for myself;
I felt alone and frightened; no one seemed to understand.
Then my mother found me words that came from deep inside:
"You have a voice; it is your song".
This truth has set free all those who thought they had lost theirs forever - and helped them find what's truly beautiful about themselves again!

author: stephen_crane
text:
When I heard those words, I laughed at first. Then my face was serious as ever before, and I looked around me again.
The walls and ceiling had become covered with some sort of pale yellow dust; everything lay there without any sound or movement, but still it seemed alive. The house itself--the old man's house--had been empty for years; the whole place was silent and deserted.

author: stothert_james_a
text:
But, when my soul looks down to these last-born hills

And sees them all for once, they know not how

To do their work again : nor could they try

With that dull labour which the gods assign

author: thomas_hardy
text:
There was once an old woman, with a cat
 Whose name it was Trixie; she had many fat
 Rabbits in her cellar ; so did not miss

 The price that the neighbours paid for meat to kiss :
 Then one day at noon-tide they found her lying dead ;
 And there lay beside her dear little Trixy ;
 But lo! when his dinner was all done and ready,
 Poor Puss sat down on his mistress's bony lid !

Haiku

My wife and I are not one, but two;
We may be opposites, but we complement each other.
In love and life we're bound together.

This is an example of how a Haiku can sound:

The road was long and winding with no destination ahead
A man stood still gazing at the ocean, waiting for someone to come along
He heard it, so he turned around.

author: stothert_james_a
text:
Here lies the source of the divine light,

A beacon for us all throughout time's night;
The allure beckoning souls en masse,

To come and find their path within this place.

Through these ethereal currents we are drawn,
United by the energy within the dawn.
Our hearts resonate with each other's beat,

Binding our spirits together in sweet release.

This space where minds converge, we explore,
Uniting past, present, and future forever more.

author: stothert_james_a
text:
Thus will they say : ' The Day of Resurrection — ’

A day when never shall be heard again
The sound of weeping and the tearful sigh,
Or joy unspeakable nor man's vain strain.

In this dread hour their joys are not so sweet ;
Their hearts have ceased from earth’s unquiet pain ;
Each hath his rank assigned, and each knows well
His portion from the Lord Omnipotent.

author: thomas_hardy
text:
'The moon is yellow with desire,

 And I am black as the night;

 So I come to thee, my lady fair,

 Forth from thy shadow on the white.'

Where flowers bloom and trees are tall

text:

author: william_wordsworth
text:
And now, if yet my lips should not speak of thee,

But with some hidden thought be touched and moved

With thy sweet name, remember I am here—

author: buchanan_robert

text:
Basho's "The Lake" (1685) is one of his most popular haiku, written while he was an exile during the Japanese Civil War. In it Basho uses simple language to convey deep feelings about nature and life:

A drop falling into water makes a sound; so too does a leaf fall from a tree.
But no two sounds are alike—each has its own individuality and character.
Like raindrops in a lake, we pass through our lives with grace and beauty, but at last come together.

author: william_wordsworth
text:

Inspired by the words of Samuel Johnson (1709-84), we shall endeavor to weave together a tapestry of verse that resonates deeply within our souls, reflecting upon the beauty and wonder of our beloved country, Australia.

author: william_wordsworth
text: In the distant lands where time fades into eternity, beneath the celestial glow of twilight, rests the star known to us all—the mighty Sun, once a fiery luminary. A symbol of our planet's resilience and vitality, its beams cast shadows upon the earth, igniting landscapes and nurturing lives. From the depths of ocean floors to mountaintops, each breath we take owes gratitude to this cosmic guardian. So, let us raise our voices to honor the brilliance of the Sun, for without it, darkness would conquer all.
